newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VILLA ACTS TO BEAT LASER DANGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VILLA ACTS TO BEAT LASER DANGER.

text.p: English premier league soccer club Aston Villa has acted to stop a potentially dangerous new crowd trend -- the use of hand-held lasers.
Towards the end of last year Villa officials noticed the beams of light shining from the crowd and apparently aimed at the dugout.
Stewards could not find the culprit but after several more occurrences did track down someone using the pen-sized product and removed it.
The lasers, of the type used by lecturers, are not considered dangerous in themselves but there is concern that they could affect the concentration of players or officials, leading to accidents.
Villa printed a warning in its programme for the last two matches and crowd safety officer John Hood says it appears to have done the trick.
"It's becoming a new thing and we didn't want it to happen at Villa Park," Hood said.
"It could be irritating and interfering but we've had no problems in the past few games so hopefully it's gone away."
The English Football Association said on Wednesday it had not directly encountered the problem to date.
"At the moment it's not something we are concerned about and we hope it stays that way," an F.A. spokesman said.
